newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians report progress with Israel on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians report progress with Israel on Hebron.

text.p: PLO officials reported progress on Monday in talks on a long-delayed Israeli pullback from Hebron and American-Israeli-Palestinian efforts were focused on closing a deal in time for Christmas.

U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross flew to Cairo to brief Egypt on progress made in two days of talks, and Jibril Rajoub, head of Palestinian Preventive Security in the West Bank, when asked if they could finish on Monday, said: "I hope so."

The officials said there was agreement on some major disputed points, but other issues were left to be resolved in a meeting yet to be arranged between Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"The two teams and the Americans, led by Ross, met with Arafat until dawn and we can finally say there was progress," said a PLO official who declined to be identified.

U.S. Consul General in East Jerusalem, Edward Abington, said Ross would return on Monday after briefing the Egyptians. Israel Radio said in an unconfirmed report that Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa might arrive with Ross were there to be a signing ceremony later on Monday.

Israel and the PLO have accused each other of foot-dragging in more than three months of talks on the West Bank town of Hebron, 80 percent of which was due to have been handed over to Arafat's Palestinian Authority months ago. Netanyahu has demanded security guarantees for the 400 Jewish militants in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs.
